Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-11
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood Reliability), Marta (BlueBridge Head of ML), Owen (BlueBridge Platform), Lydia (BlueBridge Security), Rajiv (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Onboarding gating items mostly cleared; KMS and VPC peering still in flight.
- Night benchmark run showed improved median latency with KV cache but a P95 tail spike when batch size > 32.
- Discussed fallback plan to smaller quantized model for burst traffic; BlueBridge asked for quality/accuracy checks.
- Action items: KMS checklist, sample terraform, run logs, autoscaler policy proposal.

Topics:
- Access / creds / KMS integration status
- Benchmark results recap (median vs P95, batching, KV cache impact)
- Tuning suggestions (quant profiles, batching caps)
- Security and audit logs, SOC2 points
- Next steps and scheduling a quality deep-dive

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: all right everyone thanks for squeezing this in, uh we wanted to do a quick weekly sync on the pilot, mostly unblock items and the benchmark retrospective. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Marta: good, thanks, we're looking to close the KMS flow this week, got some questions on key rotation policy.
[00:17] Lydia: yes, we need to confirm that the HSM-backed keys can be used for request signing, and we want audit events to go to our SIEM, um so sampling of events is important.
[00:29] Priya: thanks, Lydia. quick note: our KMS integration doc includes an HSM pattern and sample rotation policy, but we can trim it to only what you need for POC. i'll paste the shortened checklist after the call.
[00:40] Owen: status on VPC peering — yesterday we could not complete the route table updates because of an overlapping CIDR. we've provisioned a transit-gateway workaround but need guidance on NLB health checks.
[00:55] Samir: if you're going transit-gateway route, the NLB health-checks need the internal IP CIDR reachable; i'll share an ingress snippet that avoids NAT and preserves keepalives.
[01:05] Rajiv: quick item from product — we're tracking latency and accuracy, but we need to see the end-to-end traces (frontend->redwood->model) so we can triage where the spikes come from.
[01:18] Jordan: perfect, we asked you to upload the prom + jaeger artifacts from the night run, did those come through?
[01:24] Owen: uploaded prometheus tar and a few jaeger spans to the S3 bucket last night, object names look like bb-pilot-20280110-*. logs show median generation at ~38 ms per token for model v1x, with P95 around 190 ms at peak traffic. but there's a clear tail after 20:30 UTC.
[01:45] Priya: that tail usually correlates with batch-size growth and kv cache misses; when the prefix is different we see cache-miss cascades. did the run enable prefix caching?
[01:55] Owen: yes we had prefix caching on but the test included a set of long instruction prefixes which invalidated a chunk of the cache at once.
[02:06] Priya: okay that explains it. two levers — cap the batch size at 24 for critical endpoints and enable partial KV warming for the top 50 prompt prefixes. we'll share a script to pre-populate the KV.
[02:20] Marta: about accuracy — when you suggested quantized model fallback for bursts, do we have a delta matrix? we need to know which intents degrade and by how much.
[02:32] Priya: we ran an internal quality check across 500 prompts. 4-bit quant (q4) had ~1.8% drop on our intent-preservation metrics, mostly around multi-step reasoning prompts. 8-bit q8 was negligible. i'll attach the data but recommend q8 for burst fallback.
[02:50] Rajiv: is the fallback automated in the routing policy? like if latency > p95 threshold route to q8 variant?
[02:57] Jordan: yes, we can set a routing rule: if P95 > 150 ms or queue depth > X then route to the compatible quantized variant in the same region. that's also how we do cross-model fallback for capacity constraints.
[03:10] Lydia: any security implications switching to q8? keys remain the same?
[03:15] Priya: tokens and encryption remain unchanged; model variant is just a different binary. KMS is used for request payload encryption at rest and for audit signing, so no change there.
[03:25] Owen: one weird trace: around 20:31 there's a synchronous retry from the app layer which doubled requests briefly; that's likely what pushed batching to the limit. we'll revisit retry logic.
[03:36] Marta: great, so for risk mitigation we should adjust the app retry jitter and add a circuit breaker on 429s before the fallback policy kicks in.
[03:45] Priya: agreed. also suggest a soft cap on multiplexer batching — i can provide a config that limits token aggregation per endpoint.
[03:56] Jordan: Samir, can you walk through the autoscale suggestion you mentioned in the notes?
[04:00] Samir: sure. given BlueBridge's traffic profile, i'd recommend a small dedicated pool for baseline, plus a burst tier on shared capacity. autoscaler policy: scale up aggressively to burst when queueing > 150k tokens and scale down after 10m of idle at 25% capacity. i'll send numbers in a short doc.
[04:18] Owen: will that change our cost expectations? we need an estimate of token cost delta for the three-tier model.
[04:24] Jordan: we'll recalc cost with the dedicated baseline + burst model and include a 30% buffer for network egress and transformer overhead, send by monday.
[04:33] Rajiv: small ask — can we get the per-route token breakdown? so product and finance can model spend per feature.
[04:39] Jordan: yes, Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdown; i'll export a CSV for you.
[04:45] Marta: back to KMS — Lydia, will the simplified checklist be enough for SOC2 evidence for the POC?
[04:52] Lydia: for POC, yes. for full prod we'll need key rotation evidence, HSM attestation, and audit trail retention policies. but checklist is fine to proceed.
[05:02] Priya: i'll include exactly which audit event names we emit so you can map to your SIEM.
[05:07] Owen: about ingress — Samir's NLB snippet should avoid rewrite loops, please send it.
[05:12] Samir: will do. also note: if you use the transit-gateway workaround, keep healthchecks shallow and use sticky session for the management plane.
[05:22] Marta: quality deep-dive — we want to prioritize intents A, B, C for the quantization matrix. can we get a 45-minute session next week?
[05:29] Priya: yes, i'm available Tue or Thu next week, will propose slots.
[05:34] Jordan: last thing — contract/price: we made a small tweak to the pilot pricing for the dedicated baseline, i'll email the redline and the updated pilot summary by EOD tomorrow.
[05:45] Rajiv: thanks, that's helpful.
[05:48] Lydia: one more note on audit logs: retention needs to be at least 90 days for now — is that configurable in the console?
[05:54] Priya: retention is configurable per-tenant, yes. we'll show a quick walkthrough in the next call.

(occasional crosstalk and filler omitted)

Wrap / Recap (auto-gen):
- KMS/HSM steps: Priya to provide trimmed checklist and sample IAM/KMS policy.
- Benchmark artifacts: Owen to upload run logs and traces (prom + jaeger) — Samir and Priya to analyze tail causes.
- Autoscaler policy: Samir to deliver draft.
- Fallback model recommendation: Use q8 for burst fallback; q4 may degrade multi-step reasoning (~1.8% metric drop).
- Next meeting: schedule quantization/quality deep-dive (Priya + Marta) and follow up on the night-run analysis.

Links referenced: S3 bucket: s3://bb-pilot-uploads (Owen), KMS doc (will be shared in follow-up), Redwood pilot pricing sheet (Jordan to send).

End of transcript.
